_source: Modern MBA long video 'How Microsoft Wasted $113 Billion on Xbox', 651K views, 45.8 min. Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-19 (speed pass per owner): frames at 0.3/3/8/15/25/40/55 s, then seeks at 291-297.5 (chart burst)/300/700/1250 (sponsor)/1800/2400/2735 s; captions read on the frames (manual, about 160-170 words a minute). No audio probe on this one. Our own descriptions; shots after 60 s are spot samples.

lines.gist: Sets up 20 years of three companies fighting console wars.
Says electronics leaders rarely stay on top for long.
Each leader slipped and a rival rose; one entrant paid billions to join.
That entrant set the modern online multiplayer standard.
Built from off-the-shelf parts, each console sold at a loss.
Another few years of losses was too dangerous to bear.
An all-or-nothing gamble to save the boss and reach the mass market.
Now it can earn from players on rivals' devices too.
Each was forced to innovate, which handed consumers the win.

ending.lastFrame: archival store footage into a YouTube end screen

whyItWorks: The title's figure is the frame for 45 minutes; the film walks generation by generation like an industry history.
Archival launch events and period gameplay put the viewer in each year without any narrator on camera.
A few dense, bold data cards (one word title, two-colour bars, product photos as axis labels) carry the key economics.
Unit economics explained per item (price vs loss per console) make a billion-dollar number feel concrete.
